subject: Archaeology
title: Nineveh: The Assyrian War Machine
description: A fast breakdown of Nineveh: The Assyrian War Machine for builders.

hook.text: The Assyrian Empire ruled through terror. Wall carvings at Nineveh showed impaled prisoners and flayed skin hung on.

buildup.text: Nineveh was the largest city in the world by 700 BCE. Its walls stretched 7.5 miles and enclosed palaces, gardens.

discovery.text: Austen Henry Layard excavated Nineveh in the 1840s, shipping massive winged bull statues to the British Museum.

twist.text: The terror propaganda may have been exaggerated. The Assyrians also built libraries, hospitals, and botanical gardens.

climax.text: Nineveh fell dramatically in 612 BCE. A coalition of enemies sacked it so thoroughly that the city was lost for 2,000.

punchline.text: The most feared empire in the ancient world was erased so completely it took.

quiz.question: What happened to the Assyrian capital of Nineveh?
options: It was gradually abandoned as the climate changed
A coalition sacked it so thoroughly in 612 BCE that it was lost for 2,000 years
It was buried by a massive sandstorm and sealed until modern times
